Fixed / Warranty - Drivers - 2026/09/14 11:00 CST - Notes by Gemini

# Quick notes

## Fixed / Warranty - Drivers

Sep 14, 2026

Cristian Arizmendi (cristian.arizmendi@driverdo.com), Julia Diaz (julia.diaz@draiver.com), Juliana Turin (juliana.turin@driverdo.com), Armando Flores (armando.flores@driverdo.com), Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade (rafael.andrade@draiver.com)

Warranty program review with compliance risks and algorithmic alternatives.

## Fixed driver program and regulatory compliance

- The program pays drivers 800 pesos daily across 5 or 6 weekly days.
- Juliana Turin flagged that guaranteeing wages within 12 days risks reclassifying drivers as employees.
- Experienced drivers handle complex Kavak operations and generate 5 to 7 daily movements.

## Algorithmic incentive models and platform compliance

- Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade noted that mandating presence at client facilities violates platform requirements.
- Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade proposed using historical data to pre-allocate trip volumes.
- Discussed implementing Uber-style tier categories or algorithmic criteria instead of direct client assignments.

## Next steps

- [Julia Diaz, Cristian Arizmendi] Develop Driver Model: Create an incentive system that adheres to digital platform regulations by using algorithmic criteria instead of fixed workplace requirements. Utilize the concept of pre-allocated tasks to achieve productivity goals.
- [Julia Diaz, Cristian Arizmendi] Pitch Technical Implementation: Share the finalized logic with the product and engineering teams to evaluate feasibility and implementation.

# Full notes — Sep 14, 2026

## Fixed / Warranty - Drivers

### Summary

Warranty program review with compliance risks and algorithmic alternatives.

**Warranty program compliance risks**
Discussion on fixed daily driver payments revealed potential employee reclassification risks under digital platform labor laws.

**Operational rationale and risks**
Experienced drivers ensure high productivity but mandating fixed schedules threatens platform status.

**Algorithmic incentives and integration**
Proposal to build algorithm-based logic for open platform drivers to ensure regulatory compliance.

### Decisions

## Needs Further Discussion

- **Algorithmic restructuring of driver warranty program** The team deliberated transitioning the driver warranty program to an algorithmic, criteria-based model open to all drivers to comply with digital platform regulations, with final proposals pending further development and consultation with product and tech teams.

### Next steps

- [Julia Diaz, Cristian Arizmendi] Develop Driver Model: Create an incentive system that adheres to digital platform regulations by using algorithmic criteria instead of fixed workplace requirements. Utilize the concept of pre-allocated tasks to achieve productivity goals.
- [Julia Diaz, Cristian Arizmendi] Pitch Technical Implementation: Share the finalized logic with the product and engineering teams to evaluate feasibility and implementation.

### Details

- **Overview of the Fixed Warranty Driver Program in Mexico**: Julia Diaz (00:00:00) introduces a warranty program operating in Mexico with specific drivers (00:01:34), where participants receive a base of 800 pesos per day, working five to six days a week for a total of 4,000 pesos weekly (00:04:40). Julia Diaz explains that because this arrangement resembles a fixed salary, they want to rename the program from "fixed drivers" to avoid compliance risks, treating it instead as a standard program where drivers earn money based on daily work (00:03:00).
- **Legal and Compliance Risks of the Driver Program**: Juliana Turin states that they were previously unaware of this daily driver arrangement. Juliana Turin (00:03:00) points out that under digital platform labor laws updated the previous year, drivers reaching minimum monthly wage thresholds within a limited timeframe (such as 12 days) must be registered as employees rather than independent contractors. Furthermore, Juliana Turin (00:04:40) notes that requiring drivers to stay from 9:00 a.m. until all trips are finished lacks the autonomy and discontinuity required for independent contractor status.
- **Operational Rationale for Using Experienced Kavak Drivers**: Julia Diaz (00:07:49) explains that Kavak relies on these specific, trusted drivers because they are highly familiar with Kavak's complex operational processes. Unlike new drivers who might become frustrated, these experienced individuals consistently achieve five to seven movements per day and have worked with Kavak for years (00:09:12). Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade (00:07:49) questions why these drivers need to be assigned to specific days, prompting Julia Diaz to emphasize that this familiarity and reliability are essential for maintaining high productivity (00:09:12).
- **Platform Status Risks and Alternative Demand Modeling Proposals**: Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade warns that mandating drivers to work for a specific client on fixed days threatens the status as a digital platform, cautioning that it risks turning the service into a traditional transportation company. To address this, Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade suggests training more drivers or implementing a demand-based "fake trips" model using historical data — similar to a restaurant anticipating ingredient needs — where predictable trips are created without car details initially and populated closer to the time of execution (00:10:27). Julia Diaz (00:12:49) notes that while this mirrors the approach of other outsourcing companies working with Kavak, they wanted to find a balanced model that maintains high vehicle movement productivity while respecting digital platform requirements.
- **Algorithm-Based Incentives and Open Platform Requirements**: Cristian Arizmendi proposes adopting an Uber-style model where drivers receive earnings guarantees if they meet specific trip objectives. Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade (00:15:23) distinguishes Uber's approach by noting it applies platform-wide through the algorithm, whereas hand-picking ten specific drivers for a closed program violates algorithmic platform requirements. Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade recommends collaborating with product and tech teams to build logic into the algorithm — such as category levels like gold and platinum — so opportunities are open to all drivers (00:17:13). Julia Diaz (00:18:21) highlights a potential downside, noting that open-platform drivers may lack familiarity with Kavak's specific processes or interest in working exclusively for them.
- **Compliance Guardrails and Next Steps for Tech Integration**: Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade (00:19:48) clarifies that while weekend work is permitted, the critical rule is that the algorithm cannot mandate presence at a specific client's facility, as this establishes a fixed workplace. Rafael Pagliuso De Andrade reiterates the value of the demand-based trip generation approach to manage volume safely. Julia Diaz (00:20:51) concludes by agreeing to account for these compliance constraints, consult with the technology team, and propose a workable solution for Kavak operations.
